questions.answer: Ja, en čaj in eno vodo.
questions.answer_en: Yes, one tea and one water.

questions.answer: Ja, imamo bel in črn kruh.
questions.answer_en: Yes, we have white and dark bread.
No, today we don't have any croissants.

questions.en: Do you have a brother or a sister?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I have a brother and a sister.
My brother is five years old.
No, I don't have a dog. I have a cat.
My school is in the centre.

questions.en: Shall we go for an ice cream?

questions.answer: Ne, ne razumem. Ali lahko ponovite?
questions.answer_en: No, I don't understand. Can you repeat that?

questions.answer: Ja, eno solato in pol kile sira.
questions.answer_en: Yes, one lettuce and half a kilo of cheese.

questions.sl: Ali gre ta avtobus v center?
questions.en: Does this bus go to the centre?
questions.answer: Ne, ta gre na železniško postajo.
questions.answer_en: No, this one goes to the railway station.
Number six goes to the centre.
A glass of apple juice, please.

questions.answer: Danes imamo dobro juho in ribe.
questions.answer_en: Today we have good soup and fish.

questions.en: What are you doing on Saturday?
questions.answer_en: On Saturday I'm going to the mountains.
No, I don't have my book.
No, I don't understand the exercise.
I know. The answer is five.

questions.en: Can I go to the toilet?
What do we have first lesson?
Can you lend me a pencil?
Shall we go to the playground after school?
What was the weather like yesterday?

questions.answer_en: Yes, I have it in my bag.

questions.answer: Na Krvavec ali v Kranjsko Goro.
questions.answer_en: To Krvavec or to Kranjska Gora.

questions.answer: Na začetku ja, potem pa je zabavno.
questions.answer_en: At the beginning yes, but then it's fun.

questions.en: Are you coming with us on Saturday?
questions.answer_en: With pleasure, but I don't have skis.

w01-d01-s02.note: ste is 'you are', when speaking politely or to several people.

w01-d01-s03.note: 'And you?' is pa vi. Plain 'and' is in.

w01-d01-s05.note: Slovenian needs the verb: jaz sem, I am. You can drop jaz, but never sem.

w01-d01-s06.note: Literally 'how to you is name'. The little words vam and je normally sit in second position.

w01-d01-s10.note: After v, meaning 'in', the ending changes: Ljubljana becomes v Ljubljani.

w01-d02-s01.note: Izvolite is what staff say to invite your order. It also means 'here you are' when handing something over.

w01-d02-s02.note: When you ask for something, the ending changes: ena kava becomes eno kavo.

w01-d02-s03.note: After z, meaning 'with', the ending changes: mleko becomes z mlekom. And ali means 'or'.

w01-d02-s05.note: še is 'more' or 'still'. kaj is 'what', and also 'something'.

w01-d02-s06.sl: Ja, en čaj in eno vodo.
w01-d02-s06.en: Yes, one tea and one water.

w01-d02-s08.note: With five or more, the ending changes: pet evrov.

w01-d03-s01.note: jutro is morning. Careful: jutri means tomorrow.

w01-d03-s02.note: Here ali opens a yes or no question. And Slovenian uses a normal verb for 'to have': imam, imate.

w01-d03-s03.sl: Ja, imamo bel in črn kruh.
w01-d03-s03.en: Yes, we have white and dark bread.

w01-d03-s05.note: rogljiček is a little horn, a croissant.

w01-d03-s06.en: No, today we don't have any croissants.
w01-d03-s06.note: nimamo is 'we don't have'. After it the ending changes: rogljički becomes rogljičkov.

w01-d03-s07.note: Slovenian has a special form for exactly two of something: dva bureka.

w01-d03-s08.note: bo is 'will be'. Shop staff ask Bo to vse: will that be all?

w01-d03-s10.en: Thank you, and have a nice day!

w01-d04-s01.en: Do you have a brother or a sister?
w01-d04-s01.note: imaš is 'you have', said to a friend. To an adult you say imate.

w01-d04-s02.en: Yes, I have a brother and a sister.
w01-d04-s02.note: After 'I have', brat becomes brata and sestra becomes sestro.

w01-d04-s03.note: sta is 'the two of them are'. Slovenian has special forms for two people. For three or more it would be so stari.

w01-d04-s04.en: My brother is five years old.
w01-d04-s04.note: leto is a year. pet let: five years.

w01-d04-s05.note: Here pa means 'and as for'. Three and four years are leta; five and more are let.

w01-d04-s06.en: Do you also have a dog?

w01-d04-s07.en: No, I don't have a dog. I have a cat.

w01-d04-s08.note: tvoja is 'your', said to a friend. šola is school.

w01-d04-s09.en: My school is in the centre.

w01-d05-s01.note: ura is both hour and clock. Literally 'how much is the hour'.

w01-d05-s03.note: čas is time in general. An hour is ura.

w01-d05-s04.note: After nimam, 'I don't have', the ending changes: čas becomes časa.

w01-d05-s07.en: Shall we go for an ice cream?
w01-d05-s07.note: greva is 'the two of us go'. With three or more people it is gremo. And sladoled is ice cream.

w01-d05-s09.note: Clock times use ob: ob petih, at five.

w01-d05-s10.note: se vidiva means 'the two of us see each other'.

w02-d01-s01.note: Languages end in o here: slovensko, angleško, nemško.

w02-d01-s02.note: učim se is 'I am learning'. Without the little word se, učim means 'I teach'.

w02-d01-s04.en: Thank you. I speak English and German.

w02-d01-s06.note: 'Can' is the word lahko plus a normal verb: lahko ponovite, you can repeat.

w02-d01-s07.note: počasi is slowly. počasneje is more slowly.

w02-d01-s09.sl: Kako se to reče po slovensko?
w02-d01-s09.en: How do you say that in Slovenian?

w02-d01-s10.note: ni problema is 'no problem'. Dobro vam gre is literally 'it goes well for you'.

w02-d02-s02.note: After an amount, the ending changes: jabolka becomes kilo jabolk.

w02-d02-s04.note: stane is 'costs'. solata is lettuce as well as salad.

w02-d02-s05.note: The special form for two: dva evra. Five was pet evrov.

w02-d02-s06.sl: Dobro, eno solato in pol kile sira.
w02-d02-s06.en: Good, one lettuce and half a kilo of cheese.

w02-d02-s09.note: After s, meaning 'with', the ending changes: kartica becomes s kartico. s and z are the same word; the next sound decides which one you use.

w02-d03-s01.sl: Oprostite, ali gre ta avtobus v center?
w02-d03-s01.en: Excuse me, does this bus go to the centre?
w02-d03-s01.note: Going to a place is v center. Being in a place is v centru.

w02-d03-s02.sl: Ne, ta gre na železniško postajo.
w02-d03-s02.en: No, this one goes to the railway station.
w02-d03-s02.note: železniška postaja is the railway station. A bus stop is just postaja.

w02-d03-s03.en: Number six goes to the centre.

w02-d03-s05.note: na desni is on the right. On the left is na levi.

w02-d03-s07.note: čez with a time means 'in': čez pet minut.

w02-d03-s08.note: vozovnica is a ticket for transport.

w02-d04-s01.note: A table is miza. A chair is stol.

w02-d04-s02.en: Here you are. Here is the menu.
w02-d04-s02.note: jedilni list is the menu, literally 'eating sheet'.

w02-d04-s03.note: This is the future: boste pili, you will drink.

w02-d04-s04.en: A glass of apple juice, please.
w02-d04-s04.note: kozarec is a glass. jabolčni sok is apple juice.

w02-d04-s06.sl: Danes imamo dobro juho in ribe.
w02-d04-s06.en: Today we have good soup and fish.

w02-d04-s07.note: When ordering, bom on its own means 'I'll have'.

w02-d04-s08.note: Vam je všeč is literally 'is it pleasing to you'. That is how Slovenian says 'do you like it'.

w02-d04-s09.note: The little word je comes second: zelo je dobro.

w02-d05-s04.en: What a pity! I don't like rain.
w02-d05-s04.note: škoda is 'what a pity'. After 'I don't like', the ending changes: dež becomes dežja.

w02-d05-s05.en: What are you doing on Saturday?
w02-d05-s05.note: Days use v: v soboto, on Saturday.

w02-d05-s06.en: On Saturday I'm going to the mountains.
w02-d05-s06.note: grem is 'I go'. hribi are the hills or mountains.

w02-d05-s08.sl: Z očetom. Mama je pri babici.
w02-d05-s08.en: With my dad. Mum is at grandma's.
w02-d05-s08.note: oče is father. 'With dad' is z očetom.

w02-d05-s10.en: I wish you a nice weekend!
w02-d05-s10.note: ti is 'to you', informal. The usual reply is hvala, enako: thanks, same to you.

w03-d01-s01.note: usedite se is 'sit down', said to several people or politely to one.

w03-d01-s02.en: Open your books at page ten.
w03-d01-s02.note: odprite is 'open'. knjiga is a book and stran is a page.

w03-d01-s03.en: Sorry, I don't have my book.
w03-d01-s03.note: After nimam, the ending changes: knjiga becomes knjige.

w03-d01-s04.en: No problem. Share with your classmate.
w03-d01-s04.note: sošolec is a classmate. glej k sošolcu is literally 'look towards your classmate'.

w03-d01-s05.en: Can I go to the toilet?
w03-d01-s05.note: stranišče is the toilet. Ali lahko grem is 'may I go'.

w03-d01-s07.note: naloga is a task or exercise. Homework is domača naloga.

w03-d01-s08.note: kdo is who. odgovor is the answer.

w03-d01-s09.en: I know. The answer is five.

w03-d01-s10.note: pravilno means correct. Wrong is narobe.

w03-d02-s01.note: živijo is 'hi' among friends. Kako si is how you ask a friend. To an adult it is Kako ste.

w03-d02-s02.note: v redu means okay or fine.

w03-d02-s03.en: What do we have first lesson?
w03-d02-s03.note: At school, ura is a lesson. prva ura is the first lesson.

w03-d02-s04.note: School subjects: matematika, angleščina, slovenščina. After 'we have', matematika becomes matematiko.

w03-d02-s05.note: This is the past: si naredil, you did, said to a boy. To a girl it is si naredila.

w03-d02-s06.note: ampak is but. težka is hard or difficult.

w03-d02-s07.en: Can you lend me a pencil?
w03-d02-s07.note: svinčnik is a pencil. posodiš is 'you lend'.

w03-d02-s08.note: izvoli is 'here you are' to a friend. To an adult it is izvolite.

w03-d02-s09.en: Shall we go to the playground after school?
w03-d02-s09.note: po šoli is after school. igrišče is a playground or sports ground.

w03-d03-s02.en: Yes, and the wind is blowing.
w03-d03-s02.note: veter is wind. piha is 'it blows'.

w03-d03-s03.note: včeraj is yesterday. je bilo is 'it was'.

w03-d03-s04.note: sneg is snow. bo snežilo is 'it will snow'.

w03-d03-s05.note: mislim is 'I think'. Literally: I think that yes.

w03-d03-s06.note: rad imam is 'I like', said by a boy. A girl says rada imam.

w03-d03-s07.note: imam raje is 'I prefer'. poletje is summer.

w03-d03-s08.note: poleti is 'in summer'. vroče is hot, and prevroče is too hot.

w03-d03-s09.note: dežnik is an umbrella, from dež, rain.

w03-d03-s10.en: Thanks, I have it in my bag.
w03-d03-s10.note: ga is 'it' or 'him'. torba is a bag.

w03-d04-s01.note: znaš is 'you know how to'. smučati is to ski.

w03-d04-s02.note: zima is winter. vsako zimo is every winter.

w03-d04-s03.note: kam is 'where to'. After 'go', the verb drops its final i: smučati becomes grem smučat, I go skiing.

w03-d04-s04.sl: Na Krvavec ali v Kranjsko Goro.
w03-d04-s04.en: To Krvavec or to Kranjska Gora.
w03-d04-s04.note: Two well-known ski resorts. Notice it is na Krvavec but v Kranjsko Goro.

w03-d04-s05.note: deskati is to snowboard. deska is a board.

w03-d04-s07.sl: Na začetku ja, potem pa je zabavno.
w03-d04-s07.en: At the beginning yes, but then it's fun.
w03-d04-s07.note: na začetku is 'at the beginning'. zabavno is fun.

w03-d04-s08.en: Are you coming with us on Saturday?

w03-d04-s09.en: With pleasure, but I don't have skis.

w03-d04-s10.sl: Ni problema, lahko si jih izposodiš.
w03-d04-s10.en: No problem, you can rent them.
w03-d04-s10.note: izposoditi si is to borrow or rent. jih is 'them'.
